questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Chilika Lake:
1. Chilika Lake is located to the south of the Narmada delta.
2. It is Asia’s largest brackish water lagoon and India’s first Ramsar wetland site (1981).
Which of the above statements is/are incorrect?
questions.solution: Statement 1 is incorrect. Chilika Lake is located south of the Mahanadi Delta in Odisha, not the Narmada delta. Statement 2 is correct.

questions.question: Delhi ridge is the water divide between which of the following rivers?
questions.solution: The Delhi Ridge serves as a major water divide between the Ganges and Indus river systems. It prevents the waters of the two major basins from mixing.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the canal systems and Doabs of Punjab:
1. The Bist Doab Canal System lies between the Sutlej and Beas rivers.
2. The Makhu Canal System, built in 1950, draws water from the Sutlej river.
3. Doab Bari lies between the Beas and Chenab rivers.
Which of the statements given above is incorrect?
questions.solution:
Statement 3 is incorrect. The Bari Doab is located between the Beas and Ravi rivers (not Chenab).

The major Doabs of Punjab are:
  • Bist Doab: Between Beas and Sutlej.
  • Chaj Doab: Between Chenab and Jhelum.
  • Rechna Doab: Between Ravi and Chenab.
  • Bari Doab: Between Beas and Ravi.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of Indian rivers is west flowing?
questions.solution: The Narmada and Tapi are the two major west-flowing rivers of Peninsular India. They flow through rift valleys and drain into the Arabian Sea. Other west-flowing rivers include the Periyar and Sharavathi.

questions.question:
Match the following dams with the rivers on which they are built.
a. Hirakud Dam(i) Chambal river
b. Nagarjuna Sagar Dam(ii) Narmada River
c. Sardar Sarovar Dam(iii) Krishna River
d. Tehri Dam(iv) Mahanadi river
e. Rana Pratap Sagar dam(v) Bhagirathi river
questions.solution:
The correct matches are:
  • Hirakud: Mahanadi (iv)
  • Nagarjuna Sagar: Krishna (iii)
  • Sardar Sarovar: Narmada (ii)
  • Tehri: Bhagirathi (v)
  • Rana Pratap Sagar: Chambal (i)

questions.question: Which of the following rivers is joined by river Chambal from the south?
questions.solution: The Chambal River is a major right-bank tributary of the Yamuna. It joins the Yamuna from the south in Uttar Pradesh. The Yamuna itself is the largest tributary of the Ganga.

questions.question:
Choose the coasts that are running along the Arabian sea.
A. Northern Circars, B. Malabar, C. Konkan, D. Coromandel
questions.solution: The Konkan and Malabar coasts are located on the western side of India along the Arabian Sea. The Northern Circars and Coromandel coasts are located on the eastern side along the Bay of Bengal.

questions.question: Which river flows into the Wular lake in the north and then into Baramulla?
questions.solution: The Jhelum River originates at Verinag, flows through Wular Lake, and passes through Baramulla before entering a deep gorge in the Pir Panjal range.

questions.question: Which river originates from ‘Rakshastal north-western tip’ near Mansarovar?
questions.solution: The Sutlej River (ancient name Shatadru) originates from Rakshastal in Tibet. It enters India through the Shipki La pass and is the only Indus tributary that starts outside of India.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding drainage patterns in India:
1. Radial drainage pattern is formed when rivers discharge their waters into a central depression or lake, as in Loktak Lake (Manipur).
2. Centripetal drainage pattern is formed when rivers originate from a hill and flow in all directions, as in the case of Narmada.
Which of the above statements are incorrect?
questions.solution:
Both statements are incorrect because the definitions are swapped:
  • Centripetal: Rivers flow toward a central depression (e.g., Loktak Lake).
  • Radial: Rivers flow outward from a central high point in all directions (e.g., Narmada from Amarkantak).

questions.question: In which of the following districts is Baira Siul Dam located?
questions.solution: The Baira Siul Dam is located in the Chamba district of Himachal Pradesh. It is a major hydroelectric project utilizing the waters of the Baira, Siul, and Bhaled tributaries of the Ravi river.

questions.question:
Choose the correct statement about the peninsular rivers.
A. The Narmada rises in the Malwa plateau.
B. The Godavari rises from the slopes of the Western Ghats near Nashik.
C. The Mahanadi rises in the highlands of Chhattisgarh.
D. The Krishna rises from a spring near Mahabaleshwar.
questions.solution: Statements B, C, and D are correct. Statement A is incorrect because the Narmada originates from the Amarkantak Plateau in Madhya Pradesh, not the Malwa plateau.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s water treaties with its neighbours:
1. The Farakka Treaty (1996), signed with Bangladesh, relates to the sharing of Ganga waters.
2. The Mahakali Treaty (1996) was signed between India and Pakistan.
Which of the above statements is incorrect?
questions.solution: Statement 2 is incorrect. The Mahakali Treaty was signed between India and Nepal (not Pakistan). The water treaty between India and Pakistan is the Indus Waters Treaty (1960).

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about River Ganga?
questions.option_1: River Ganga flows from the Himalayas all the way to the Bay of Bengal.
questions.option_2: River Ganga in India is more than 2500 km long and is the most populated river basin in the world.
questions.option_3: River Ganga and its river basin support lots of wonderful wildlife, particularly river dolphins, otters, freshwater turtles, and gharials.
questions.option_4: The water level of River Ganga never depends on monsoon and climatic condition of the Himalaya.
questions.solution: Statement (d) is incorrect. The water level of the Ganga strongly depends on both the monsoon rains (July-October) and the melting of Himalayan glaciers.

questions.question: In which district of Uttarakhand does the Ramganga river originate from the Doodhatoli ranges?
questions.solution: The Ramganga river originates in the Pauri Garhwal district of Uttarakhand from the Doodhatoli range. It flows through the Jim Corbett National Park before joining the Ganga near Kannauj.

questions.question: The drainage basin of the Godavari river is present in which of the following states of India?
questions.option_1: Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu
questions.option_2: Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, and Odisha
questions.option_3: Chhattisgarh, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Kamataka, and Tamil Nadu
questions.option_4: Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Odisha
questions.solution: The Godavari basin covers Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, and parts of Karnataka. It is the largest peninsular river basin in India.

questions.question: Identify the dam that is located in South India.
questions.solution: The Mettur Dam is located in Tamil Nadu (South India) on the Kaveri river. Gandhi Sagar is in Madhya Pradesh, Tilaiya is in Jharkhand, and Rihand is in Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: Which east-flowing river basin covers the states of Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Orissa and has a drainage area of 39,033 sq km?
questions.solution: The Brahmani River is the second largest river in Odisha and its basin extends over Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha. It is formed by the confluence of the Koel and Shankh rivers.

questions.question: Which ports belong to the western coast of India?
questions.option_1: Kandla port, Mormugao port, Kochi port
questions.option_2: Kandla port, Mormugao port, Chennai port
questions.option_3: Kandla port, Mormugao port, Kolkata port
questions.option_4: Kandla port, Haldia port, Kochi port
questions.solution: The major ports on the West Coast include Kandla (Gujarat), Mumbai, JNPT (Maharashtra), Mormugao (Goa), New Mangalore (Karnataka), and Kochi (Kerala).

questions.question: Dihang and Lohit are rivers in which of the following regions?
questions.solution: Dihang and Lohit are rivers in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. The Brahmaputra is known as the Dihang in Arunachal Pradesh, and the Lohit is one of its major tributaries.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding major ports of India:
1. Kandla Port (Deendayal Port), located in the Gulf of Kutch (Gujarat), was developed in the 1950s after Independence to ease pressure on the Mumbai Port.
2. Visakhapatnam Port was developed after Independence to replace Karachi Port, which went to Pakistan during partition.
Which of the above statements is incorrect?
questions.solution: Statement 2 is incorrect. Kandla Port (not Visakhapatnam) was the port developed to replace the loss of Karachi Port to Pakistan after partition. Visakhapatnam is a natural harbor on the East Coast.

questions.question: Which river basin originates from the Western Ghats range of Karnataka state and has many tributaries such as the Noyyal, Kabini, Arkavathi and Amaravati?
questions.solution: The Kaveri (Cauvery) river originates at Talakaveri in the Western Ghats of Karnataka. Its tributaries include the Kabini, Arkavathi, Noyyal, and Amaravati.

questions.question: Which of the following lakes is the longest in India?
questions.solution: Vembanad Lake in Kerala is the longest lake in India, stretching over 80 km. It is famous for the Nehru Trophy Boat Race and its extensive backwater network.

questions.question: Which river from the following flows through a rift valley?
questions.solution: The Tapi (along with the Narmada) flows through a rift valley created by tectonic activity between the Satpura and Vindhya ranges.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Beas River:
1. The Beas River, a tributary of the Indus, originates near the Rohtang Pass at an altitude of about 4,000 meters.
2. Its ancient name was Vipasha.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. The Beas River originates at Beas Kund near the Rohtang Pass and was known as Vipasha in Vedic times.
